column1: Code changes - what was deployed, when, and what it added to the schema

Lab convention: every column on the metrics sheets traces to the build that introduced it. Sizes are byte counts read off the files inside each backup, and the 'New globals' column is derived by diffing the <Data name=...> declarations between consecutive backups' .dtx files - not from memory. 'No motion changed' means no speed, no motion descriptor and no pick/place logic was altered - instrumentation and flow control only. One caveat: the CycleTiming build's own .dtx is inside a zip that is not extracted here, so its 20 new globals are first OBSERVED in the 2026-09-01_14h00m .dtx; the byte size (23,850 -> 29,089 at 2026-08-26_14h58m) is what dates them to that build.

tkBeltScan.pgx (14,017) runs the detector scan in parallel with the pick, at priority 35. AperaOwnSocket.pgx (5,669) is the single socket-ownership handshake - apera_send holds ONE unlocked socket, so two tasks writing to it can interleave and read each other's reply.

column6: tkBeltScan given private result arrays, and the branch-B and FoV counters added. It had been writing nCountPlatesFound, and because it stops on the first plate it always wrote 1 - making bLastPart true on every following pick, self-sustaining (22 consecutive belt kicks in the log). Also killed the absorbing bScanDone state and the double-trigger race.

column1: Built and reverted, not deployed - recorded so it is not repeated:

Conditional waitEndMove() in Part_Accept (flow control): a PART-DROP HAZARD. dioSet(dDOemh_gripperOFF,1) fires before tGripperEMH("OFF"), and movej/movel only QUEUE motion. There is no waitEndMove() between tkCycle's retreat waypoints and the Part_Accept call, so that waitEndMove is the task-to-motion-queue synchronisation point. Removing it would release the plate in flight over the belt. Reduced speed does not help - it drops the plate from a slower arm at the same wrong place.

mNomSpeed leave/reach 50 -> 10: wrong, and for a recorded reason. The controller's own stock template (usr/templates/default/default.dtx) has leave=50 reach=50 accel=100, so that move could already blend. The change would have tightened both corners of the plate-carrying move about 5x while raising acceleration 44% - the worst combination for a magnetically held plate, and the opposite of the smoothing asked for. Left at defaults.
